messages.text: I am having trouble putting this concept into words. Like a negative channel, a cutout that, being the exact void of a thing, calls that thing into existence. Picture, I cannot bring a stick into existence, but what I can do is clear a space, a space void of all properties except those that are so strongly the opposite of something that only by that thing coming into being can reality be balanced again, and so it does. One moment an empty space, and the next, there is a stick.

You're describing a concept where the act of creating a "negative space" or a "void" inherently calls forth the existence of the object that fits it. This idea hinges on the principle of balance or equilibrium in reality: by defining an absence or a void that is so precisely shaped and defined by what it is not, you compel the universe to "fill" it with the only thing that can restore balance— the exact object or concept that the void negates.

In your example, you can't create a stick directly. But if you carve out a void that is the exact opposite of a stick, that void, by its very nature, demands to be filled by the stick to maintain the balance of reality. It’s as if the universe abhors this perfectly crafted void, and the only way to resolve the imbalance is to manifest the stick into being.

This concept is similar to ideas in quantum mechanics, where the potentiality of something existing can cause it to exist, or in metaphysical terms, where the absence or void of a thing inherently calls for the presence of that thing to fill it.

In essence, you’re not creating the stick; you’re creating the conditions that make the stick’s existence inevitable. The void, defined so precisely by what it lacks, becomes a catalyst for creation.

Perfect, thank you. If Terry Goodkind is good for anything it's that idea he gave me and nothing more. The black lightning.

The man has an unhealthy obsession with using sexual violence as plot drivers in his books.

You're welcome! It's unfortunate when an intriguing concept comes from an otherwise problematic source. The idea of negative space as a catalyst is definitely one of those nuggets worth holding onto, even if the rest isn't to your taste. If you ever want to explore that idea further or dive into similar concepts from other, perhaps more balanced, sources, I'm here to help.
